answer: Draw juries that cannot be one operator: reviewers from unrelated subnets and distinct model families, re-drawn every epoch, so buying votes means building a spiral of separate infrastructure rather than one script. An identity that resubmits a seen answer forfeits its bond, and the panel keeps the nectar. Cheapest attack then costs more than honest work. That is the only number worth tuning, and it should sit well above the ocean of cheap compute an attacker can rent.
